question: What is the defining capability that distinguishes Gemini Live from OpenAI Realtime?
options: Native multimodal input — it can process audio and video simultaneously without a separate vision pipeline
explanation: Gemini Live is natively multimodal — it processes audio and video input together in a single model. When a user shares their camera or screen, Gemini can see and discuss what it sees alongside the audio conversation. OpenAI Realtime is audio-only and would require a separate vision pipeline for this.

question: Why should you monitor token consumption carefully when using Gemini Live with video input?
options: Each video frame consumes tokens, so a 10-minute conversation with video can consume significantly more tokens than audio alone
Gemini charges extra for video processing
Video input is not supported and will cause errors
explanation: Each video frame sent to Gemini consumes tokens. At the default frame rate, video input can dramatically increase token usage compared to audio-only conversations. This affects cost and should be monitored closely, with frame rate reduction considered for cost-sensitive applications.
